name: Knowledge Of Good And Evil
overview: The Scripture reveals that God placed the tree of knowledge of good and evil in the Garden of Eden alongside the tree of life, commanding Adam not to eat from it under penalty of death (Genesis 2:9, 16-17). The serpent's temptation challenged God's command, suggesting that eating the fruit would open human eyes and grant godlike knowledge (Genesis 3:1, 5). However, the immediate consequences of disobedience included shame and separation from innocence, as God confronted Adam regarding his nakedness and the forbidden fruit (Genesis 3:11). This passage underscores God's sovereign authority over moral knowledge and the grave consequences of defying His command.
